Maria G.: Heads-up — Kevin flagged an incoming contract ask from ACME: they want a contractual SLA of 99.95% uptime + a p95 inference latency <= 50ms for their us-west workloads. Sales says it's a hard requirement to close the deal. :eyes:
Alex S. (Support): Noted. They opened a support ticket too (INC-8421) asking for an implementation plan and fallback behavior during incidents.
Kevin L. (Sales): Confirming — customer will only sign enterprise with that SLA and 24/7 P1 support. They are willing to pay for Dedicated capacity but want SLA baked into the contract.
Priya N. (Eng-SRE): 50ms p95 across general-purpose models in us-west is optimistic on current shared fleet. For Redwood Dedicated with pinned model variants and locality we could approach it for small request sizes, but depends on batching, quantization, and instance type. Need perf profile + token distribution.
Maria G.: Ok — we need a deterministic intake + triage flow so sales/support don't promise things. Proposal: create an "SLA Intake Playbook" doc + a short form to capture constraints. Quick draft fields below:
```
- customer_name
- contract_id / opp_id
- requested_uptime (e.g., 99.95)
- latency_target (metric + percentile)
- target_region(s)
- workload_profile (qps, median tokens, max tokens)
- model(s) to be served
- expected ramp timeline
- willingness to pay for Dedicated / Reserved
- required support hours / response SLA
```
Alex S. (Support): Love the form. Suggest adding "fallback policy" checkbox (auto-fallback to lower SLO model, degrade to best-effort) and contact for escalation.
Priya N. (Eng-SRE): Also need to capture traffic shape (burstiness) and tail-latency SLAs. For routing we need to know if they permit multi-region failover.
Daniel R. (Legal): From contract side, we'll need clear definitions: what counts as downtime (control plane vs inference errors), measurement window, remedies, and cap on liability. We'll draft standard clauses once product defines measurable SLOs.
oncall-bot: A runbook placeholder "sla-acme-1769004523" was created by Maria G.
Maria G.: Proposed triage matrix (quick):
- Priority A (high risk contract): If uptime >=99.9 OR latency <100ms and customer requires 24/7 support -> route to Product + Eng-SRE + Sales; require Dedicated capacity feasibility study within 3 business days.
- Priority B: negotiated SLA or longer timeline -> Product + Solutions engage; feasibility within 10 business days.
- Priority C: informational -> standard backlog.
Kevin L. (Sales): Can we add pricing delta grid? e.g., Dedicated small pool + SLA add-on = +X% ARR. Sales needs ballpark to negotiate.
Priya N. (Eng-SRE): I'll run a quick feasibility sweep: give me sample QPS and token dist. If they opt for Dedicated, we can propose an architecture: pinned model on DGX-like instances, direct routing from us-west, reserved capacity with autoscale buffer. I'll post perf estimates in this thread.
Maria G.: Action items: 1) Kevin — fill intake form and attach perf sample by EOD tomorrow (1769080923). 2) Priya — feasibility note + rough cost delta within 48h. 3) Daniel — draft contract template items and list open legal questions. 4) Alex — link INC-8421 and tag customer comms template.
Alex S. (Support): Done — linked the ticket and added customer message draft.
Kevin L. (Sales): I'll fill the form now and ping once uploaded. :thumbsup:
Priya N. (Eng-SRE): Starting perf sweep. If we need sub-50ms p95 we might require quantized models + node-local KV caches and aggressively tuned batching. Early expectation: achievable but at material cost.
Maria G.: Thanks all. We'll reconvene once Priya posts numbers. Please don't promise SLA to the customer until Product signs off.
Daniel R. (Legal): Noted. I'll wait for product-defined metrics before drafting clauses.
Maria G.: tagging @Priya N. for updates. :memo:
